newsitem.title: UK: Former ally Jovic denounces Serbia's Milosevic.
newsitem.headline: Former ally Jovic denounces Serbia's Milosevic.

text.p: Ex-Yugoslav president Borisav Jovic has denounced his former ally Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic and said his tough stance would wreck the government.

In an interview with The Guardian newspaper that was published on Friday, Jovic urged Milosevic to accept municipal election defeats and reduce the influence of his wife in the country's political life.

"If someone thinks they can do anything against the regulations of his party, against the constitution and the law, that is a very serious situation," Jovic said in the interview, conducted in Belgrade.

Serbia's president has adopted a low profile as tens of thousands of people have taken to the streets of Belgrade to protest against the annulment of November local elections which handed victory to the opposition.
Jovic blamed the crisis largely on the influence of Markovic's wife Mirjana.

"The problem is (president) Milosevic is elected by the people but she is not elected by anybody...In practical terms, a lot of decisions are made by her. That is a completely abnormal situation," Jovic told the newspaper.
